Logic: 'we cannot park cars there, but we can stop to pick up passengers' is exactly the US/NYC legal meaning of a 'No Standing' sign (a vehicle regulation permitting brief passenger pickup/drop-off but no waiting or parking). It is consistent with every narrative fact: the friend stopped her car at that corner to pick Carol up, and her 'Of course you can stand there' shows the sign does not govern pedestrians. This resolves the misunderstanding the anecdote is built on.

Grammatical, but introduces conditions with zero textual license: nothing in the passage mentions avoiding an entire avenue or a lunch-hour restriction. A 'No Standing' sign posted at one corner cannot entail avenue-wide avoidance. Fabricated content; indefensible.

Her explanation cannot condemn her own just-completed action. Indefensible.

Contradicts the pragmatic force of her laughter and reassurance. Indefensible.
